title: OpenTelemetry
description: OpenTelemetry is an open-source observability framework. It provides APIs, libraries, and tools to capture distributed traces and metrics from .NET applications.

data.text: OpenTelemetry is a vendor-neutral observability framework. It provides a single set of APIs, SDKs, and tools to collect distributed traces, metrics, and logs from your application and export them to any backend.

data.title: Installation
data.content: Install the OpenTelemetry packages for ASP.NET Core.
data.code:
dotnet add package OpenTelemetry.Extensions.Hosting
dotnet add package OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.AspNetCore
dotnet add package OpenTelemetry.Exporter.Console

data.title: Configuring OpenTelemetry
data.content: Add tracing and metrics to an ASP.NET Core app.

terms.definition: A representation of a request as it moves through a distributed system, composed of spans.
A single unit of work within a trace, representing one operation or service call.
A component that sends telemetry data to a backend such as Jaeger, Zipkin, or Prometheus.

data.title: Vendor Neutrality
data.text: OpenTelemetry avoids vendor lock-in. You can switch from Jaeger to Zipkin or the OpenTelemetry Collector without changing your application code.
Traces, Metrics, and Logs Under One Standard

OpenTelemetry is a vendor-neutral standard for the three signals. The application emits traces (spans across services), metrics (counters and histograms), and logs; an exporter ships them to whatever backend you choose. Because the instrumentation is standard, changing the backend does not change the code.

data.title: Wiring traces and metrics with ASP.NET Core instrumentation
data.content:
builder.Services
    .AddOpenTelemetry()
    .ConfigureResource(r => r.AddService("Orders.Api"))
    .WithTracing(tracing => tracing
        .AddAspNetCoreInstrumentation()
        .AddHttpClientInstrumentation()
        .AddEntityFrameworkCoreInstrumentation()
        .AddOtlpExporter())
    .WithMetrics(metrics => metrics
        .AddAspNetCoreInstrumentation()
        .AddHttpClientInstrumentation()
        .AddRuntimeInstrumentation()
        .AddOtlpExporter());

// A custom span for a business operation
using var activity = Activity.Current?.Source.StartActivity("ProcessOrder");
activity?.SetTag("order.id", orderId);

data.title: Interview angle: context propagation is the whole point
data.text: A trace is only useful if the same trace id crosses every service, so the W3C `traceparent` header is forwarded on outgoing calls and every log line carries the trace and span id. That is what lets you follow one request through five services and the logs they produced. When asked how you debug a distributed failure, the answer is a trace id in the logs, not more log lines.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: It captures traces, metrics, and logs
Exporters send data to backends like Jaeger, Prometheus, and the Collector
data.takeaway: OpenTelemetry is the future of observability in .NET, replacing proprietary SDKs.

data.title: Exercise: Trace a Distributed Request
data.description: Instrument two services with OpenTelemetry and visualize the trace.
steps: Create two minimal APIs: ServiceA and ServiceB
Add OpenTelemetry to both with ConsoleExporter
Run both services and call ServiceA
Observe the trace spans in the console output
data.expectedOutcome: Console exporter shows a trace with spans for ServiceA and the outgoing call to ServiceB.
